extracted.intended_audience: vehicle manufacturers, safety engineers, regulatory counsel, and other parties petitioning NHTSA for temporary exemptions from FMVSS No. 108 (adaptive driving beam/headlamp stakeholders)
extracted.subtask_description: Criteria and procedural standards NHTSA uses to evaluate petitions for temporary exemptions from FMVSS No. 108 to allow adaptive driving beam (ADB) headlighting systems, including applicable FMVSS provisions and information petitioners must provide. Focused on whether exemptions are necessary given a newly promulgated final rule and whether petitioned systems meet safety-equivalence and performance requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Temporary exemption statutory basis (49 CFR 555.6(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: The basis for both petitions is that an exemption would make easier the development or field evaluation of a new motor vehicle safety feature providing a safety level at least equal to that of the standard. 49 CFR 555.6(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petitions should demonstrate that a temporary exemption will facilitate development or field evaluation of a new safety feature and that the feature will provide a safety level at least equal to the relevant FMVSS requirement. NHTSA evaluates petitions against this statutory criterion when deciding whether to grant temporary exemptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: S9.4 — Means of switching between lower and upper beams
rubrics_metrics.description: Section S9.4 requires that a vehicle have a means of switching between lower and upper beams. The means must be designed and located so that it may be operated conveniently by a simple movement of the driver's hand or foot. The switch must have no dead point and, except as provided by S6.1.5.2, the lower and upper beams must not be energized simultaneously except momentarily for temporary signaling purposes or during switching between beams.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petitioners seeking exemption from S9.4 must explain how their ADB systems interact with this switching requirement (e.g., whether simultaneous energization occurs and why). Provide technical descriptions showing operation, user control/location, and measures addressing convenience and absence of a 'dead point.'

rubrics_metrics.name: S10.14.6 — Photometry requirements for integral beam headlighting systems
rubrics_metrics.description: S10.14.6 specifies the photometry requirements for integral beam headlighting systems, including minimum and maximum photometric intensities of the upper beam light.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petitions requesting exemption from S10.14.6 should identify which photometric requirements the system cannot meet, provide measured photometry, and explain how the system's performance nevertheless provides an equal level of safety (for example, through dynamic beam shaping that reduces glare while improving visibility).

rubrics_metrics.name: ADB performance requirements: prevent glare and provide minimum visibility
rubrics_metrics.description: The final rule establishes performance requirements to ensure that ADB systems operate safely by not glaring other motorists and providing a minimum level of visibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluation focuses on whether the ADB system meets the final-rule performance metrics for glare prevention and minimum visibility. Petitioners should document system performance with respect to glare control (to other motorists) and objective measures of driver visibility. NHTSA notes these requirements are generally within capabilities of current ADB systems, though system modifications may be necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Demonstration of safety equivalence and supporting information
rubrics_metrics.description: Petitioners explained how their systems operate and the safety benefits they believe the system would offer, and submitted additional information in response to NHTSA's requests to assist evaluation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Effective petitions include clear descriptions of system operation, claimed safety benefits (e.g., improved pedestrian/cyclist/object illumination), supporting data or test results, and responses to any requests for additional information. NHTSA considered petitioners' arguments and submitted comments and information in its analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provision of requested supplemental information
rubrics_metrics.description: NHTSA requested additional information from Volkswagen, BMW, and any other manufacturers wishing to submit exemption petitions for ADB systems, to assist NHTSA in evaluating such petitions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petitioners must respond to agency requests for additional information; failure to provide requested data may weaken the petition. Responses submitted in reply to such requests are considered in the agency's evaluation (and may also be considered in related rulemaking dockets).

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of public comments and external submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: NHTSA received and considered comments from manufacturers, trade groups, public interest groups, and individuals when reviewing the petitions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The agency considers stakeholder comments (supporting and opposing) in its evaluation. Petitioners should anticipate and address likely public and industry concerns; submitting supporting comments or technical endorsements may be relevant to the agency's assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: No exemption when final rule renders it unnecessary
rubrics_metrics.description: NHTSA determined that, in light of the publication of a final rule amending FMVSS No. 108 to allow ADB systems, there is no need to grant the requested exemptions because the standard now allows the deployment of such systems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a final rule already authorizes the technology (and sets applicable requirements), NHTSA will typically find a temporary exemption unnecessary. Petitioners should assess whether existing or imminent regulatory action already addresses the need the petition seeks to fulfill.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public interest consideration when deciding exemptions
rubrics_metrics.description: NHTSA stated it would not be in the public interest to exempt the ADB systems from the requirements for ADB systems in the final rule based on the information provided in the petitions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Granting an exemption is weighed against the public interest; petitions must show that exemption would not harm public safety or otherwise be contrary to the public interest. Exemptions that would undercut final-rule protections or public-safety objectives are disfavored.
